73ae98fa97.q: Why are mosquitoes attracted to beer drinkers and breweries?
73ae98fa97.a: Mosquitoes are attracted to carbon dioxide, which is released both when humans breathe and when beer ferments or is poured. In breweries, CO2 from fermenting beer tanks with airlocks constantly releases into the cellar, attracting mosquitoes through open doors. Beer drinkers are also more susceptible to mosquito bites because the bubbles released when pouring beer into a glass or drinking from a can attract the insects just as exhaled CO2 does.

16c9f77501.q: What chemical compound in beer attracts fruit flies during fermentation?
16c9f77501.a: The compound isoamyl acetate, which produces a banana flavor, is present in many beers during fermentation. This same chemical is a sex pheromone for fruit flies, making them think it is mating season when they smell it. This banana flavor is particularly strong in beers like Coors Banquet and German Hefeweizen, which is why these styles attract significant numbers of fruit flies.

e80bda97f3.q: How does the Guinness widget create the creamy foam in the can?
e80bda97f3.a: The Guinness widget is a ping pong ball with a hole in it placed inside the can before sealing. Just before the lid closes, one drop of liquid nitrogen is added and the lid is sealed. When the can is opened, the pressure drops and beer rushes out through the tiny orifice in the widget, nucleating bubbles inside the can and creating the signature creamy foam when poured.

3cc475b9aa.q: What happened when Tilray acquired Ten Barrel Brewing?
3cc475b9aa.a: Tilray, a cannabis company, acquired Ten Barrel Brewing. Within a year of the acquisition, Tilray announced layoffs and eliminated the entire innovation team at Ten Barrel. This was particularly significant because Ten Barrel's employees, including award-winning brewmaster Tanya Ewing, had been excited about the new ownership opportunity away from AB InBev, only to face job cuts shortly after.

4d9c5f58f3.q: Why did Sugar Creek Brewing rebrand the Big O can after 10 years, and what design changes were made?
4d9c5f58f3.a: The rebrand moved away from a busier design with gears to a cleaner aesthetic that still retained the integrity of the original product. The new can features mountains like Grandfather Mountain and Mount Mitchell, incorporates the Wright Brothers logo since Sugar Creek recently rolled out in the Outer Banks, and shifted from a glossy to a matte finish to work better with modern LED-lit grocery store displays. Eric and Joe designed the can themselves through several iterations and added a blood orange contrast to better reflect the actual flavor profile of the beer.

326bb2158c.q: What is the Big Hazy O blend at Sugar Creek Brewing and how is it produced?
326bb2158c.a: The Big Hazy O is a blended beer created by combining the Big O blood orange ale with the Unlimited Juice hazy IPA in a 50-50 ratio. The idea originated from customers in Sugar Creek's tap room who would blend the two beers themselves. In production, they take a fresh Big O and a fresh hazy and blend them 50-50 before canning, allowing customers to get the same tap room experience in a can. Reviews for the commercially blended version have been even better than each beer on its own, demonstrating the one-plus-one-equals-three concept.

86a7d3b64e.q: Why does Sugar Creek Brewing use etched glasses with hidden designs at the bottom?
86a7d3b64e.a: The etching at the bottom of Sugar Creek's glasses, including the Wright Brothers plane, serves a functional purpose called nucleation that brings bubbles up and maintains a nice foam layer on top of the beer. The foam layer is critical because it prevents the beer from getting oxidized, releases the aroma, and provides texture and mouthfeel. While Sugar Creek initially tried to give custom branded glassware to tap room patrons following Belgian brewery tradition, the company lost approximately $35,000 in stolen glassware in its first year, forcing them to limit these special glasses to special occasions or retail sales.
